title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (pages 744–746 of the continuation of La Longue Marche). M is a 0-connected 'multiplicité' (in modern terms a Deligne–Mumford stack, or orbifold curve) over a field k. It is of finite type, geometrically smooth, of dimension 1. On the previous page Grothendieck conjectured that M is a quotient (U,G) = [U/G]: a smooth quasi-projective curve U with an action of a finite group G, the stack being the ringed topos of G-equivariant étale sheaves on U.

This page states a stronger, 'more intriguing' expectation. M should admit a finite étale cover, which may be taken Galois with group G, whose total space U is a scheme. U would then necessarily be a smooth quasi-projective curve over k, so M = [U/G] with U → M étale. In modern terms this asks that every orbifold curve be uniformizable by a scheme through a finite étale cover.

Assuming this, he fixes a geometric base point a and identifies π := π_1(M,a) with the equivariant fundamental group π_1(U,G;a) (formula (10)). He then restricts to characteristic 0, first with k algebraically closed. There is an exact sequence (11): 1 → Π_0 = π_1(U,a) → π_1(U,G;a) = π → G → 1. Π_0 is the profinite fundamental group of an affine or projective smooth curve. It carries its natural 'L-structure' (structure de lacets): the conjugacy classes of cuspidal inertia subgroups and generators at the punctures.

This L-structure transports to an L-structure on π. The next page asserts that it is independent of the choice of the Galois étale cover U and of the lift of a, and that π_1(M,a) will tacitly carry it. For a general k (most interestingly finitely generated over Q), the sequence 1 → π_1(M_kbar) → π_1(M) → Gal(kbar/k) → 1 makes the geometric fundamental group an L-group with an outer Galois action. The goal is the 'universal' case of the moduli stacks M_{g,ν}.

This is part of the profinite extension of his L-group / LT-group formalism (exterior homomorphism germs T → π), aimed at the anabelian and Grothendieck–Teichmüller study of orbifold curves and moduli stacks.
errors: The expectation that every 0-connected smooth 1-dimensional DM stack over an algebraically closed field of char 0 admits a finite étale cover by a scheme is false for 'bad' orbifolds. Examples are the teardrop (P^1 with one orbifold point, the weighted projective line P(1,n)) and the spindle P^1 with two orbifold points of unequal orders. These are not uniformizable by a finite étale cover; the teardrop is even simply connected as a stack.

For the same bad orbifolds, the presentation (9) M = [U/G] with U a curve and G finite fails as well. They are quotients only by G_m-type groups, as in Behrend–Noohi's uniformization of DM curves. A hypothesis such as hyperbolicity or 'good orbifold' is needed, which is the Fuchsian-group / Bundgaard–Nielsen–Fox theorem.
Grothendieck explicitly marks the claim as a supposition ('Supposons en tous cas qu'il en soit ainsi'), so this is an unproved and over-general hope rather than an asserted theorem.

The claim that the induced L-structure is independent of the choices is plausible: Galois covers form a cofiltered system and conjugation by π permutes the cusp classes. It is stated without proof ('manifestement').

ideas.what: Every 1-dimensional orbifold curve (DM stack) is a quotient [U/G] of a smooth quasi-projective curve by a finite group, ideally with U → M finite étale.
ideas.modern_name: Uniformization of orbifold curves / global quotient presentation of DM curves
ideas.usually_credited_to: Bundgaard–Nielsen and Fox (torsion-free finite-index subgroups of Fuchsian groups, 1950s); Behrend–Noohi, 'Uniformization of Deligne–Mumford curves' (2006); Kresch–Vistoli (2004) for finite flat covers in general
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses moduli multiplicities and their fundamental groups. An explicit statement there is unsure; it appears in the Longue Marche manuscripts.

ideas.what: Identification π_1(M,a) ≅ equivariant fundamental group π_1(U,G;a), with the extension 1 → π_1(U) → π → G → 1.
ideas.modern_name: Étale fundamental group of a quotient stack / orbifold fundamental group
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (SGA1 descent formalism); Noohi, 'Fundamental groups of algebraic stacks' (2004); Zoonekynd
ideas.where_published: SGA1 (Galois categories); used in Esquisse d'un programme for π_1 of M_{g,ν}

ideas.what: Transport of the natural cuspidal 'L-structure' (conjugacy classes of inertia lacets) from π_1 of a Galois étale cover to the orbifold fundamental group, independent of choices. Then an outer Galois action on the geometric π_1 respecting this structure, over fields finitely generated over Q.
ideas.modern_name: Cuspidal inertia structure / 'π_1 with peripheral structure' of hyperbolic orbifold curves; outer Galois representations on orbifold fundamental groups
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Longue Marche, Esquisse); developed by Ihara, Nakamura, Mochizuki (cuspidal subgroups), Hoshi–Mochizuki
ideas.where_published: La Longue Marche (1981, circulated) treats discrete L-groups (groupes à lacets); the profinite orbifold version is unsure

missed.claim: Grothendieck formulates the uniformizability of orbifold curves by a finite étale Galois scheme cover as a conjecture and proceeds conditionally. The question is settled in the literature: true for hyperbolic or good orbifolds, false for teardrops and spindles.
missed.quote: Plus intriguant, il doit être vrai qu'il existe un rev. étale fini de M (galoisien pour simplifier, de groupe G) qui soit un schéma algébrique
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical only: it shows Grothendieck anticipating the Behrend–Noohi / Kresch–Vistoli type results within the anabelian program. No new mathematics.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a conditional setup: uniformizability of orbifold curves, the equivariant π_1 extension, and transport of the cuspidal L-structure. All of these are now standard (Fuchsian group theory, Noohi, Behrend–Noohi, Mochizuki/Nakamura). The overly general uniformization hope is a minor historical curiosity.
transcription_corrections: In (10), (11) and the last line, the second group is most likely π_1(U,G;a), the equivariant fundamental group of U with its G-action, not π_1(M,G;a); the handwriting is ambiguous between U and M.
'et la [-L-] structure : toute intérieure[?] sur Π_0' should probably read 'et la L-structure naturelle sur Π_0'.
'se transporte[?] en une L-structure sur π = π_1(M,a), qui manifestement' is followed on the next page by '[ne] dépend pas'. The symbol is lowercase π, not Π.
'(galoisien pour simplifier, galoisien, de groupe G)': the second 'galoisien' is likely a hesitation or duplicate in the manuscript.
